item.title: Irreducible Representations as Local Maxima of a Matrix-Coefficient Functional
item.description: arXiv:2611.09972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional unitary representation of a finite group $G$ and, for unit vectors $v$, let $\Phi(v)$ be the mean of $|\langle v,gv\rangle|^2$ over $g\in G$. We show that $v$ is a local maximum of $\Phi$ if and only if the subrepresentation generated by $v$ is irreducible. Thus local maximization of $\Phi$ extracts irreducible subrepresentations of $V$ directly, with no character or isotypic projection specified in advance. The proof is elementary: Schur averaging reduces it to a singular-value calculation. The values and dimensions of the connected components of the local-maximum set determine the degrees and multiplicities of the irreducible constituents, and for $H\leq G$ the intersections of the $G$- and $H$-local-maximal loci encode branching multiplicities. We also determine the critical landscape and give a normalized gradient iteration whose generic limit generates an irreducible subrepresentation.
item.dc:creator: Pin-Chi Hung, Ming-Hsuan Kang

item.title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2611.10163v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(\lambda)$ ($\lambda$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms. The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Frank L\"ubeck

item.title: An explicit basis for the unipotent Specht modules of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each partition $\lambda$ of $n$ we construct an explicit basis of the unipotent Specht module $S^\lambda$ of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, defined recursively over horizontal strips. Each basis vector is $g\,x_\tau$, where $\tau$ is a semistandard tableau of shape $\lambda$, $x_\tau$ is obtained from a Steinberg-type vector by alternately applying a permutation matrix and a Fourier sum over a unitriangular group, and $g$ runs over an explicit set of coset representatives. Grouping the basis by the standardization of $\tau$ gives exactly $q^{\mathrm{maj}(s^T)}$ vectors for each standard tableau $s$, which is the numerical form of the Dipper-James standard basis problem. The same family is a basis over every field containing a nontrivial $p$th root of unity, including fields whose characteristic divides $|\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)|$, and a subfamily chosen layer by layer gives a basis of the simple quotient $D^\lambda$. We also give a basis of the $U$-fixed vectors of $S^\lambda$ and computed values of $\dim D^\lambda$ for $\mathrm{GL}_n(2)$.
item.dc:creator: Scott Andrews

item.title: A silting theorem for extended module categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.10849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize the silting theorem of Buan and Zhou to extended module categories. For a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{P}$ over a proper $d$-truncated non-positive dg algebra $A$, we construct a $(d+1)$-term silting object $\mathbf{Q}$ over the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra $B$ of $\mathbf{P}$. The $s$-torsion pairs induced by $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{Q}$ yield equivalences of Brenner-Butler type between the torsion class on either side and the torsion-free class on the other. There is also a dg algebra homomorphism from $A$ to the $d$-truncated dg endomorphism algebra of $\mathbf{Q}$, which is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf{P},\mathbf{P}[i])=0$ for all $i\leq-d$. Moreover, we describe Auslander-Reiten theory in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!B}$ in terms of that in ${d\text{-}\operatorname{mod}\!A}$.
item.dc:creator: Chenhui Liu, Yu Zhou

item.title: Eaton Triples, Polar Representations, and Lie Triple Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.10859v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An Eaton triple consists of a finite dimensional real inner product space, a closed subgroup of its orthogonal group, and a closed convex cone that meets every orbit and satisfies an extremal inner product inequality. In the literature on group majorization and invariant norms it is a standing hypothesis that the triple admits a reduced triple, obtained by restriction to the span of the cone. We prove that this is always the case: the axioms force the span of the cone to be a section of a polar representation, and Gichev's orbit intersection theorem applies. The reduced group is a finite reflection group, crystallographic when the group is connected; Eaton cones are its closed chambers, unique up to the group action; and a compact linear group admits an Eaton cone if and only if its representation is polar with a finite reflection group as Weyl group. For connected groups we construct a Lie triple system on the space, determined by the inner product and the orbits alone, for which the cone is a Weyl chamber; unlike Dadok's orbit equivalence with a symmetric space, it involves no choices.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Larotonda, Tin-Yau Tam

item.title: The Fourier kernel and invariant trace formula of $\rm{GL}(3)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Trace formula is an important method to study the Langlands program. Arthur obtains the existence of stable trace formula for connected reductive group. In this paper, we will give the explicit invariant trace formula of GL(3). For general reductive groups, Arthur gave an inductive proof of the existence of the invariant trace formula and provided explicit examples for GL(2). For GL(3), we successively compute the invariant distributions, give all the Fourier kernels for the GL(2) cases, and finally obtain the concrete invariant trace formula.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Wang, Xinghua Cui, Zhifeng Peng

item.title: Inhomogeneous deformations of $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$: triviality for any number of odd parameters
item.description: arXiv:2611.11153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We treat a symmetrized mixed-oscillator deformation family of the orthosymplectic Lie superalgebras $\mathfrak{osp}(N|2n)$, $N,n\geq1$, with even mixed coefficients $\beta_{u,i}$ and one odd square-zero parameter. We derive the deformed bracket from an oscillator realization, show that its coefficient is determined by the realization, and exhibit an explicit odd primitive, normalized by its vanishing on $\mathfrak{sp}(2n)$. Every odd primitive differs from it by a unique inner derivation. For $N=1$ this is the case $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$ treated earlier. With multiple odd parameters the deformed bracket is the sum of the single-parameter deformations and is again trivial. The trivialization, however, is not additive: it is the product of the single-parameter trivializations followed by a nonsymplectic change of the bosonic generators. The main results are formalized in Lean~4, with the algebras constructed by generators and relations; what is not formalized is stated in the appendix.
item.dc:creator: Hisashi Aoi

item.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_{\alpha} C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(\alpha)$ and letting $C_\alpha=\langle\alpha\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_\alpha$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[\alpha]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_\theta H$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.
item.dc:creator: Peng He, Xue-ping Wang

item.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
item.description: arXiv:2611.11363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $\Omega$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/\mu_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/\mu_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.
item.dc:creator: Yau Wing Li

item.title: Dlab--Ringel standardization in algebraic triangulated categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.11434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of derived standardly stratified algebras as a connective dg analogue of standardly stratified algebras. To this end, we extend the Dlab--Ringel standardization method to algebraic triangulated categories and show that every basic proper derived standardly stratified algebra arises from this extended method. We establish Ringel duality for derived standardly stratified algebras using silting objects. More precisely, the Ringel dual is again derived standardly stratified, and the corresponding perfect derived categories are related by mutually quasi-inverse contravariant triangle equivalences. We also show that, over an algebraically closed field, a proper derived standardly stratified algebra is smooth if and only if its derived standard modules are exceptional. Finally, we prove that dg algebras given by finite acyclic graded quivers with arrows of non-positive degrees and homogeneous relations are derived standardly stratified with respect to every total order on the vertices.
item.dc:creator: Takahide Adachi, Mayu Tsukamoto

item.title: Representations of the Weyl algebra modulo $p^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.11575v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{k}$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Let $R=W_2(\mathbf{k})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of length $2$. In this note, we are concerned with the study of representations of the first Weyl algebra that are finite-rank free $R$-modules ($R$-lattices). Our main result shows that given an $R[x]$-lattice $V$, it admits a left module structure over the Weyl algebra (equivalently, an $R$-linear connection) if and only if all of its indecomposable summands have the form $R[x]\otimes_{R[x^p]}N$, where $N$ is an indecomposable $R[x^p]$-lattice of rank divisible by $p$. We also classify, up to isomorphism, all lattices over the $p$-Weyl algebra (defined by $[y,x]=p$) for which the action of $x$ modulo $p$ is regular nilpotent.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Mamani-Velasco, Akaki Tikaradze

item.title: Presentations of inverse Artin monoids of type $D_n$ via cluster mutations
item.description: arXiv:2611.11880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $D_n^\varepsilon$ denote the Dynkin diagram of type $D_{n+1}$ with the endpoint $\varepsilon$ of its long branch frozen, and let $\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$ be the mutation class of any orientation of this diagram under mutations at mutable vertices. For each $\Gamma\in\mathcal{M}(D_n^\varepsilon)$, we define an inverse monoid $M_\Gamma$ by generators and relations determined by $\Gamma$. We prove that $M_\Gamma\cong M_{\mu_k(\Gamma)}$ for every mutable vertex $k$. Consequently, every quiver in this mutation class yields a presentation of the inverse Artin monoid of type $D_n$. Our argument establishes mutation invariance for the presentations of inverse Artin monoids of both types $A_n^\varepsilon$ and $D_n^\varepsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Bing Duan

item.title: Invariant operations on vector fields on the line are Lie polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.11900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that all $W_1$-equivariant multilinear operations on the Witt Lie algebra $W_1$ are Lie polynomials. We study this question in terms of Wronskian Lie brackets and Novikov products, which are abstractions of the Lie bracket $[a,b]:=ab'-ba'$ and the nonassociative product $a\circ b=ab'$ one can define on a commutative differential algebra. In terms of these notions, our main result asserts that the operad of Wronskian Lie algebras is isomorphic to the operad of equivariant multilinear operations on~$W_1$; we also prove a parallel result for the operad of Novikov algebras, characterizing it as the operad of affine equivariant multilinear operations on $W_1$. Two immediate consequences of our work are a characterization of Lie polynomials in free Novikov algebras and a computation of the degree zero homology of the operadic twisting of the Novikov operad. Finally, while it is known that over a field of zero characteristic, a Novikov algebra embeds into its differential envelope, we show that the same is not necessarily true for Wronskian Lie algebras.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko, Farukh Mashurov, Bauyrzhan Sartayev

item.title: From Frobenius seeds to self-orthogonal modules over symmetric algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct finite-dimensional symmetric algebras admitting nonprojective self-orthogonal modules from Frobenius algebras equipped with a module satisfying explicit stable and homological conditions. The resulting modules have complexity three, and their stable endomorphism algebras are isomorphic to the algebra of dual numbers over the ground field. The construction combines a variable input with a fixed auxiliary factor carrying the required twisting, and preserves the input through specified quotient and corner constructions. The proof combines derived induction, an obstruction to perfect factorization, and a cone construction over a Gorenstein triangular matrix algebra. For a symmetric algebra and a self-orthogonal generator, we describe the derived category of the opposite endomorphism algebra through a recollement with a two-term $2$-symmetric dg algebra. For our counterexamples, it is formal and quasi-isomorphic to an explicit four-dimensional dg algebra. Applications to cyclic coverings of a quantum exterior algebra yield connected examples with explicitly determined numbers of simple modules. The construction works over every field containing an element of infinite multiplicative order.
item.dc:creator: Hongxing Chen

item.title: Global-dimension spectra of gentle algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12492v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the connected finite-dimensional gentle algebras of finite global dimension whose global-dimension spectra under derived equivalence are not intervals of integers. These are precisely the algebras with AAG invariant $[(2,4g)]$, where $g\geq2$, whose canonical line field is induced by a nowhere-vanishing vector field. Their spectrum is $\{2g,2g+2,\ldots,4g\}$. For each $g\geq2$, there are exactly two such derived-equivalence classes, distinguished by their Arf invariant. The geometric foundation is a realisation theorem for prescribed polygon weights in arbitrary genus. For an AAG invariant $[(m_i,n_i)]_{i=1}^b$ arising from such an algebra, the global dimensions attained in its AAG fibre form the integer interval $[\max_i\lceil n_i/m_i\rceil,\max_i n_i]$. By controlling the complete line-field invariant through local ribbon-graph constructions, we determine the spectrum in every derived-equivalence class.
item.dc:creator: Wen Chang, Quanyu Tang

item.title: Classification of quasi-lisse simple affine vertex algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all noncritical levels $k$ for which the simple affine vertex algebra $L_k(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, for every finite-dimensional complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$. We prove that Fiebig's equivalence between the corresponding noncritical blocks of category $\mathcal{O}$ identifies the relevant parabolic Wakimoto modules and the homomorphisms from the corresponding universal affine vertex algebras. Combining this compatibility with a characterization of semisimple points in associated varieties, we establish that for coprime positive integers $p,q$, $L_{-h^\vee+p/q}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse if and only if $L_{-h^\vee+p/\gcd(q,r)}(\mathfrak{g})$ is quasi-lisse, where $r$ is the lacing number of $\mathfrak{g}$. The classification at the resulting levels is obtained using Drinfeld--Sokolov reduction, singular vectors and relations in the reductions of the maximal ideals of $V^k(\mathfrak{g})$. We also determine the associated varieties at the quasi-lisse levels for all $\mathfrak{g}$ of rank at most six and for $E_7$ and $E_8$.
item.dc:creator: Drazen Adamovic, Xuanzhong Dai, Kaiwen Sun

item.title: On $\mathrm{HH}^1$ of blocks of finite simple group algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a sporadic simple group, $k$ a field of positive characteristic and assume $B$ is a block of $kG$ with non-trivial defect. In this paper we prove the first Hochschild cohomology group $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is non-vanishing. Furthermore, we prove that for every wild block with abelian defect of a sporadic simple group, we have that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)$ is a solvable Lie algebra of derived length two, with non-zero maximal toral rank.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Antrobus, Lleonard Rubio y Degrassi, Can Wen

item.title: Motivic generating functions and $L$-derivatives of cohomological automorphic representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10478v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Forty years ago, Gross and Zagier proved a remarkable formula computing the central derivative of the Rankin--Selberg $L$-function of a cusp form $f$ of weight $2$ and a character of the class group of an imaginary quadratic field, satisfying the so-called Heegner condition, and deduce that the nonvanishing of the central derivative implies the nonvanishing of the corresponding Mordell--Weil rank. This formula was later generalized in various contexts and degrees, for example, by S. Zhang for $f$ of higher even weights; and by Yuan--Zhang--Zhang for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form of parallel weight $2$ over an arbitrary totally real field $F$ and $\chi$ a Dirichlet character of an arbitrary CM extension $E/F$, allowing arbitrary ramification. In this article, we prove a Gross--Zagier type formula in the context of doubling method, for $f$ a Hilbert cusp form over $F$ and $\chi$ a Hecke character of $E$ of general weights under a balancing condition, again allowing arbitrary ramification. Indeed, we even formulate a general conjecture which we call the motivic arithmetic inner product formula, for cohomological automorphic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_{2r}$ over $E$ of hermitian type of balanced weights.
item.dc:creator: Yifeng Liu

item.title: On naturality of cohomological support for small quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We apply the theory of hypersurface support by Negron and Pevtsova to prove the naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum Borel groups, with respect to restriction to Levi subalgebras. This in turn implies naturality of cohomological support of the small quantum groups for modules that lift to Lusztig's big quantum group, for instance tilting modules. This allows us to make the recent conditional classification of tensor ideals of abelian type in the category of such tilting modules unconditional.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier

item.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
item.description: arXiv:2611.10936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.
item.dc:creator: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Yiyao Huang, Arushi Katyal, Ryan Lin, Pranav Ramakrishnan, Weiya Wang

item.title: On sinks and mirrors
item.description: arXiv:2611.11660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a full rank sink recurrent cluster $\mathcal{A}$ variety, we prove that its wrapped Fukaya category is equivalent to the category of coherent sheaves on a stacky elaboration of the dual Fock-Goncharov cluster $\mathcal{X}$ variety. In particular, braid varieties for a semisimple group are mirror to the braid varieties for the Langlands dual group. Another example: for compact surfaces with no interior marked points, a least one marked point on each boundary component, and at least two marked points in total, the Fock-Goncharov moduli for SL(2) and PGL(2) are homologically mirror. The results were obtained in communion with ChatGPT Astra.
item.dc:creator: Mingyuan Hu, Vivek Shende

item.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
item.description: arXiv:2611.11677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bowman, Damian de la Fuente, Nicolas Libedinsky, David Plaza

item.title: Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of root of unity quantum cluster algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.11699v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many important families of algebras $R$ in the areas of quantum groups, quantum topology and noncommutative algebra are root of unity quantum algebras, equipped with Frobenius centers $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R) \subseteq Z(R)$ and quantum Frobenius maps ${\mathrm{Fr}} : R_{\mathrm{class}} \stackrel{\cong}{\longrightarrow} Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$. We explicitly classify the Frobenius automorphism groups ${\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R))$ and the ozone groups ${\mathrm{Oz}}(R):= {\mathrm{Aut}}(R/Z(R))$, and prove that all endomorphisms of $R$ fixing its Frobenius center $Z_{\mathrm{Fr}}(R)$ are automorphisms for all algebras $R$ that come from partial root of unity quantum cluster and upper quantum cluster algebras (which have been proved to encompass a vast majority of known quantum algebras). We prove three main theorems that give the above classification results from three different standpoints. As applications, we classify the Frobenius and ozone automorphism groups of all quantum function algebras of simple algebraic groups $G$ not of type $F_4$ or $E_8$ and all quantum unipotent cells at roots of unity for arbitrary symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras.
item.dc:creator: Yunmeng Wu, Milen Yakimov

item.title: The finite projective classification of complex spinors via momentum maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.12549v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the projective orbits of complex spinors from the point of view of the momentum map. We treat the irreducible spin modules in odd dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11 and the half-spin modules in even dimensions 2,4,6,8,10,12,14, which are the only cases with finitely many orbits. In the Clifford--Fock model, we construct representatives as sums of pure basis spinors, and the coefficients are chosen so that the representative is a critical point of the squared norm of the momentum map. The resulting momentum values in a fixed Weyl chamber distinguish the orbits. Completeness follows from Vinberg's theory of graded Lie algebras and stabilizer actions, independently of the classical spinor classifications. We recover the classical counts of 1,1,1,2,3,5 orbits in the odd cases and 1,1,1,2,2,4,9 in the even cases, and compute the projective dimension of every orbit. In dimension fourteen we also determine the closure order of the orbits, using the fact that the minimum of the squared momentum norm increases strictly under degeneration.
item.dc:creator: Bart{\l}omiej Sikorski, Adam Sawicki

item.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
item.description: arXiv:2611.12608v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $\Pi$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(\Pi)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(\eta)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(\eta)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(\eta))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.
item.dc:creator: Yu Xiao

item.title: Counter-examples to Conjectures on NCCRs via a Reductive McKay Correspondence
item.description: arXiv:2611.12679v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We disprove three conjectures appearing in Van den Bergh's plenary ICM survey, posed by De Deyn and Van den Bergh, which concern the interplay between non-commutative crepant resolutions (NCCRs) and the stringy Euler characteristic. Our counter-examples are applications of a new McKay correspondence for reductive groups that we prove in this paper, extending the classical McKay correspondence for finite groups. We obtain explicit formulas for the stringy $E$-functions of reductive quotients in terms of the Weyl group action and stringy $E$-functions of toric varieties; we also obtain an equivalent formula expressed as an integral of the age function over Weyl-fixed loci of a compact real torus. For symmetric representations, our expressions are related to arithmetic Tutte polynomials, yielding combinatorial formulas for the stringy Euler characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Satriano, Jeremy Usatine

item.title: A relative trace formula for the orthogonal Gan-Gross-Prasad model and the proof of its fundamental lemma
item.description: arXiv:2611.12724v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a comparison of relative trace formulas to study the Gan--Gross--Prasad conjecture. We unfold the relative trace formulas, match their regular orbits, and formulate the corresponding fundamental lemma and smooth transfer conjecture. Finally, we prove the fundamental lemma for the unit element of the Hecke algebra.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyu Mao, Chen Wan

item.title: Functorial Homological Mirror Symmetry for Acyclic Cluster Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.12751v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the formalism of cluster models, a class of log Calabi-Yau varieties obtained from smooth quasi-affine toric varieties by iterated affine blowups along non-toric codimension 2 centers determined by a really full rank quiver. Cluster models include the truncated cluster varieties of Gross, Hacking, and Keel with respect to really full rank quivers, all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties, and all open toric subvarieties of $\mathbb{C}^n\times(\mathbb{C}^*)^m$. We then construct mirrors to cluster models via iterated Weinstein handle attachments to toric mirrors, so that the corresponding skeleta acquire compact pieces, and we prove homological mirror symmetry for all cluster models, compatibly with freezing, deleting, and contracting vertices of the quiver. This extends toric mirror symmetry and its naturalities beyond the cotangent bundle. In particular, we obtain homological mirror symmetry for all really full rank acyclic cluster varieties. We develop this package with a view towards conjectures of Marsh, Rietsch, and Williams about mirror symmetry for Grassmannians and closed positroid varieties. Motivated by these, we also conjecture that open positroid varieties are self-mirror. Assuming a natural ansatz, we prove this for a class of positroid varieties that includes nontrivial cells in every Grassmannian and all cells in finite-type Grassmannians. Towards this end we introduce a new combinatorial input, the notion of weak $k$-booleanness for permutations and braids.
item.dc:creator: Josephine Hlavinka

item.title: FRT presentation of the $q$-Onsager comodule algebra and refined $q$-characters
item.description: arXiv:2611.12874v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a concept of counital comodule algebra $(B,\delta_B,\epsilon_B)$ over a Hopf ${\mathbb K}$-algebra $H$, where $\delta_B: B\rightarrow B \otimes H$ and $\epsilon_B: B\rightarrow {\mathbb K}$ are coaction and counit homomorphisms, respectively. This structure gives a canonical (counital) comodule algebra map $\iota_B: B \rightarrow H$. In this paper, we study in details the case $B=O_q$, and $H$ is the quantum loop algebra ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$ for ${\mathbb K}={\mathbb C}$. Here, $O_q$ is the $q$-Onsager algebra with four presentations: (i) the $q$-Dolan-Grady type; (ii) the alternating type; (iii) the root vectors type; (iv) the Drinfeld type. For $(O_q,\delta_{O_q},\epsilon_{O_q})$, in fact a 3-parameter family of counital comodule algebras, we establish a Faddeev-Reshetikhin-Takhtajan (FRT) type presentation, which is written in terms of a K-operator satisfying a reflection algebra relation. The coaction $\delta_{O_q}$ (resp. $\iota_{O_q}$) sends the K-operator to a `dressed' K-operator (resp. K-matrix) using Ding-Frenkel type L-operators of ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$; the counit $\epsilon_{O_q}$ sends the K-operator to the most general (non-diagonal) solution of the reflection equation. The FRT presentation allows to compute the image via $\delta_{O_q}$ and $\iota_{O_q}$ of the generating functions of $O_q$ for each presentation (ii)-(iv). Moreover, the images of Lu-Wang's generating functions of $O_q$ in the so-called Drinfeld second realization ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$ are obtained, as well as their images via the (ordinary) coproduct of ${}^{Dr}\!{\cal L}U_qsl_2$, which enhance two theorems by Prze\'zdziecki. Finally, we apply our FRT presentation to the construction of new type $q$-characters for ${\cal L}U_qsl_2$, in imaginary root vectors of $O_q$, refining those of Frenkel-Reshetikhin, and we explain representation-theoretic meaning of such refining.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Baseilhac, Azat M. Gainutdinov

item.title: Cohomological Mackey formula for quotient stacks
item.description: arXiv:2505.09483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we construct a restriction morphism on the critical cohomology of an equivariant Landau-Ginzburg model associated to a representation of a reductive group equipped with an invariant function. We show a compatibility formula between this restriction map and the induction map considered in earlier work in the form of a Mackey-type formula, thereby giving the critical cohomology the structure of a localized induction-restriction system. In the case of quivers, our formulas give the localized coproduct of Davison for cohomological Hall algebras of quivers with potential.
item.dc:creator: Lucien Hennecart

item.title: A depth-zero principal-series block whose Hecke algebra has a non-trivial two-cocycle
item.description: arXiv:2510.07391v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recently the authors have shown that every Hecke algebra associated to a type constructed by Kim and Yu is isomorphic to a Hecke algebra for a depth-zero type. An example in the literature has been suggested as a counterexample to this result. We show that the example is not a counterexample, and exhibit some of its interesting properties, e.g., we show that a principal series, depth-zero type can have a Hecke algebra with non-trivial two-cocyle, a phenomenon that many did not expect could occur.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey D. Adler, Jessica Fintzen, Kazuma Ohara

item.title: An Algebraic Representation Theorem for Linear GENEOs in Machine Learning
item.description: arXiv:2601.03910v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Geometric and Topological Deep Learning enhance machine learning by exploiting geometric and topological structures in data. In this context, Group Equivariant Non-Expansive Operators (GENEOs) provide a principled framework for encoding symmetries and designing efficient, interpretable neural architectures. Originally introduced in Topological Data Analysis and later adopted in Deep Learning, GENEOs unify geometric and topological approaches and include, as a special case, the operator computing persistence diagrams. Their theoretical foundations rely on group actions, equivariance, and compactness properties of operator spaces. GENEOs are defined between data spaces endowed with transformation groups, referred to as perception pairs. While previous representation results characterized linear GENEOs acting on identical perception pairs, many applications require operators between heterogeneous ones. In this work, we introduce and prove a new algebraic representation theorem for linear GENEOs acting between different perception pairs. Under mild assumptions on data domains and group actions, this result provides a complete characterization of such operators and implicitly yields a computational method to generate all linear GENEOs between two perception pairs. The proof combines tools from the theory of stochastic matrices, group actions, and invariant measures. In our paper, we also show that the space of linear GENEOs is compact and convex, making easier their use for learning and optimization. Our new theorem enlarges the applicability of GENEOs, and allows for their composition with a broader class of current architectures. We show this with an application in image reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Conti, Patrizio Frosini, Nicola Quercioli

item.title: Associated varieties of integral minimal highest weight modules
item.description: arXiv:2603.26371v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex simple Lie algebra and $L(\lambda)$ be a simple highest weight module of $\mathfrak{g}$ with highest weight $\lambda-\rho$, where $\rho$ is half the sum of positive roots. A simple $\mathfrak{g}$-module $L_w:=L(-w\rho)$ is called integral minimal if the associated variety of its annihilator ideal equals the closure of the unique minimal special nilpotent orbit. In this paper, we find that the associated variety of any integral minimal module $L_w$ is irreducible and equal to the orbital variety corresponding to a minimal-length element in the Kazhdan--Lusztig right cell containing $w$.
item.dc:creator: Zhanqiang Bai, Jing Jiang, Rui Wang

item.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Karan Choudhary, Sunil Kumar Prajapati

item.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
item.description: arXiv:2608.01474v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}
item.dc:creator: Jean Kabor\'e, Ibrahim Nonkan\'e

item.title: On a basepoint issue in the tempered dual of $p$-adic $SL(n)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.05055v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of $G = \mathrm{SL}(n,F)$. Consider the action on the discrete series of $M$ of the group of unitary unramified characters of $M$ (where a character acts by twisting). Given an orbit $\mathcal{O}$ for that action, let $W_\mathcal{O}$ be the global stabilizer of $\mathcal{O}$ in the Weyl group of $M$. We construct families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ for which the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ has no fixed point. More precisely, let $n \geq 8$ be an integer that is not prime and not equal to $9$. We attach families of orbits without fixed points to any divisor $m \geq 2$ of $n$ such that $m \;| \; q-1$ where $q$ is the order of the residue field of $F$. The Levi subgroup $M \subset G$ for the corresponding families has $m$ blocks of size $k\geq 2$ and $2$ blocks of size $m$. The core of the paper is the construction of superculpidal representations of $\mathrm{GL}(m,F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}(k,F)$ satisfying some conditions that we require to construct the families of orbits $\mathcal{O}$ that we expects. In addition, we study the fixed point problem for the dimensions $n$ that we excluded above, i.e., prime or small dimensions. We prove that there is always a fixed point under the action of $W_\mathcal{O}$ in those cases.
item.dc:creator: Marie Dautheville

item.title: Homology and higher-order intermediate categories for proper abelian subcategories
item.description: arXiv:2610.01155v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an extension-closed proper abelian subcategory of a triangulated category $\mathcal{C}$, and put $\mathcal{D}_\ell=\Sigma^\ell\mathcal{A}*\cdots*\mathcal{A}$ for $\ell\geq 1$. Assuming that $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal{C}}(\Sigma^p\mathcal{A},\mathcal{A})=0$ for $1\leq p\leq\ell+1$, we construct homology functors $H_i:\mathcal{D}_\ell\to\mathcal{A}$ for $0\leq i\leq\ell$ and prove that triangles in $\mathcal{D}_\ell$ induce natural long exact sequences in $\mathcal{A}$. If $\mathcal{C}$ is Krull--Schmidt, we introduce compatible sequences of subcategories of $\mathcal{A}$ and use them to classify the homology-determined subcategories $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathcal{D}_\ell$ that are closed under extensions and direct summands.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-Gang Wu, Xianhui Fu

item.title: Irreducibility of Verma modules for symmetrizable Kac-Moody superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.06109v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a criterion for the irreducibility of Verma modules over symmetrizable Kac--Moody superalgebras. Our main tool is the Weyl-Kac denominator identity.
item.dc:creator: Maria Gorelik

item.title: Finite Root Sums in Symmetrizable Kac-Moody Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.15923v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra with root system $\Phi$. A subset $S\subseteq\Phi$ is closed if $\alpha,\beta\in S$ and $\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ imply $\alpha+\beta\in S$. For finite and affine Kac-Moody algebras, this closure property is known to extend from pairs to arbitrary finite sums that are roots. We prove that every closed subset of the root system of any symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebra is closed under arbitrary finite sums that are roots. The proof uses real-root strings, a simultaneous separation lemma for positive imaginary roots, and a lemma on when the sum of two positive imaginary roots is again a root. As an application, we extend a necessary condition for wideness of regular subalgebras from finite and affine types to all symmetrizable Kac-Moody algebras: the symmetric closure of the roots associated to a wide regular subalgebra is the entire root system.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Douglas

item.title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
item.description: arXiv:2610.34119v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $\Omega(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense. We also identify a gap in an earlier proof of its nonstandardness and give an independent proof by determining all connected Galois covering sources of $\Omega(1)$. Together, these results disprove the implication from Euclidean type to standardness in the equivalence explicitly stated by Bocian--Holm--Skowro\'nski (2004) and Bocian--Skowro\'nski (2005). They also contradict the standardness conclusion of the Proposition in \S2.1 of Skowro\'nski (1989); its main theorem in \S1.5 assumes standardness and is not contradicted by this example.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Asashiba

item.title: Webs and exponentially large mu-coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.34982v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.
item.dc:creator: Tom Goertzen, Abel Lacabanne, Daniel Tubbenhauer, Pedro Vaz

item.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.37291v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.
item.dc:creator: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang

item.title: Exchange graphs and $\tau$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41703v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify the connected components of support $\tau$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected precisely when the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules and has Cartan rank one. There are then exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero $\tau$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra is connected. Suppose the defining partial tagged triangulation is nonempty and all its endpoints are punctures. Then the realization of the support $\tau$-tilting complex is homotopy equivalent to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Signed endpoint vectors give an explicit homotopy equivalence. Under the same endpoint hypothesis, $\tau$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates and give a surface criterion distinguishing the root sets of types $A$, $D$ and $C$. The homotopy construction also applies to Brauer graph algebras with arbitrary vertex multiplicities.
item.dc:creator: Ping He, Bo Le

item.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04514v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(\rho)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $\rho$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(\rho)$ is the $\rho(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $\Pi(\rho)$ under Scholze's functor, and $\Pi(\rho)$ is the representation associated to $\rho$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Yu Xiao

item.title: On minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ for types $B$ and $C$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra of type $B$ or $C$ over ${\mathbb C}$. Given $\kappa\in{\mathbb C}$, let $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ be the universal affine vertex algebra associated with $\mathfrak{g}$ at level $\kappa$. We characterize the weights of minimal singular vectors of $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ with respect to the generalized Cartan matrix, when $V^\kappa(\mathfrak{g})$ is not simple and $\kappa$ is not critical. Furthermore, we determine the corresponding longest Weyl elements in the Kashiwara-Tanisaki character theorem of the singular vectors.
item.dc:creator: Cuipo Jiang, Tong Wu

item.title: Highest weight category structures on $rep(B)$ and full exceptional collections on generalized flag varieties over $\mathbb Z$
item.description: arXiv:2407.13653v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a split simply connected semi-simple algebraic group scheme $\mathbb G$ over $\mathbb Z$, a split maximaltorus $\mathbb T$ in $\mathbb G$and a parabolic subgroup scheme $\mathbb P\supset \mathbb T$, this paper constructs semi-orthogonal decompositions of the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb P$ with each semi-orthogonal component being equivalent to the bounded derived category $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ of noetherian representations of $\mathbb G$. The semi-orthogonal components of those decompositions are stable under the monoidal action of $D^b(rep(\mathbb G))$ on $D^b(rep(\mathbb P))$. The decompositions depend on an arbitrarily chosen total order on the Weyl group that refines the Bruhat order. The semi-orthogonal decompositions are also compatible with the Bruhat order on cosets of the Weyl group of $\mathbb P$ in the Weyl group of $\mathbb G$. Their construction builds upon the foundational results on $\mathbb B$-modules from the works of Mathieu, Polo, and van der Kallen, and upon properties of the Steinberg basis of the $\mathbb T$-equivariant $K$-theory of $\mathbb G/\mathbb B$. As a corollary, we obtain full exceptional collections in the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on generalized flag schemes $\mathbb G/\mathbb P$ over $\mathbb Z$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Samokhin, Wilberd van der Kallen

item.title: Dividends of the BKR Equivalence: Quantifying the Dichotomy for Skyscraper Sheaves
item.description: arXiv:2509.15825v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G\subset \mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb C)$ be a nontrivial finite abelian subgroup and let $\Psi \colon D^b_G(\mathbb{C}^3) \xrightarrow{\sim} D^b(G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3))$ denote the Bridgeland--King--Reid equivalence. For every nontrivial character $\chi$ of $G$, the transform of the corresponding skyscraper sheaf at the origin has exactly one nonzero cohomology sheaf, in degree $0$ or $-1$. We study the proportion $\mathcal B_0$ of characters for which this degree is zero. Using derived Reid's recipe, we establish the sharp bounds $1/3\leq\mathcal B_0\leq1$. For isolated quotient singularities, the lower bound sharpens to $1/2$, and we exhibit an explicit family of cyclic quotients indexed by positive integers $m$ for which $\mathcal{B}_0 \to 1$ as $m \to \infty$. We show that $\mathcal B_0=1$ precisely when the fiber over the origin has dimension at most one, and relate $\mathcal B_0$ to the Picard rank of $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)$ and the number of compact exceptional divisors of the resolution $G\operatorname{-}\mathrm{Hilb}(\mathbb{C}^3)\rightarrow \mathbb{C}^3/G$. A theorem of Craw--Lin--Yamagishi translates these estimates into bounds for the coordinate facets of the $G$-Hilbert GIT chamber. We discuss how the proportion $\mathcal{B}_0$ adapts to non-abelian finite subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{C})$.
item.dc:creator: Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

item.title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
item.description: arXiv:2510.01809v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.
item.dc:creator: Ony Aubril

item.title: Conservative geometric functors via purity
item.description: arXiv:2602.14886v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a criterion for determining when a family of geometric functors is jointly conservative through the lens of purity in compactly generated triangulated categories. We introduce the notion of pure descendability and we apply it to two particular situations involving sequential limits of ring spectra.
item.dc:creator: Nat\`alia Castellana, Juan Omar G\'omez

item.title: Mutation of Theta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2603.19391v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give an account of mutation of theta functions in cluster scattering diagrams, starting with a notion of mutation that is related to, but different from, the notion of mutation defined by Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich.This different approach to mutation leads to several applications. Three of the applications simplify the process of computing structure constants for multiplication of theta functions, and these are used in another paper on cluster scattering diagrams of affine type. Notable in these three applications is the appearance of mutation symmetries and dominance regions. The other two applications have to do with pointed reduced bases, a variation on the pointed bases of Fan Qin. We give a characterization of pointed reduced bases analogous to Qin's characterization of pointed bases. All of these applications take place in a version of Gross, Hacking, Keel, and Kontsevich's canonical algebra that can be constructed for an arbitrary exchange matrix.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Reading, Salvatore Stella

item.title: Oversmoothing as Representation Degeneracy in Neural Sheaf Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2605.11178v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Neural Sheaf Diffusion (NSD) learns a task-adapted sheaf geometry for node classification. We connect the study of these learned geometries with Geometric Invariant Theory (GIT) to analyse their representation-theoretic structure and develop mechanisms for geometric control during training. Identifying cellular sheaves with representations of the incidence quiver connects direct-sum decompositions to the harmonic space and motivates the study of trivial or low-complexity summands as potential degeneration modes. We make this perspective concrete by focusing on the trivial representation: on an embedded copy, the sheaf Dirichlet energy reduces to weighted scalar graph energy. The GIT stability framework provides a criterion for excluding such copies within the semistable class. Using its moment-map characterisation of polystability, we construct differentiable surrogates that encourage the corresponding balance conditions. We identify an equal-stalk obstruction to assigning a destabilising weight to the trivial representation and show how nonuniform stalk dimensions remove it. Controlled energy-minimisation experiments reproduce trivial-component formation, while native feature-conditioned NSD experiments on heterophilic graphs show how moment-map regularisation changes the balance and Dirichlet-energy trajectories of learned geometries during training, alongside their classification behaviour.
item.dc:creator: Arif D\"onmez, Axel Mosig, Ellen Fritsche, Katharina Koch

item.title: Representation Varieties of Stacks and Trace Maps
item.description: arXiv:2609.09633v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define a derived stack $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ which generalizes the assignment $A\leadsto \operatorname{Rep}_n(A)$ to an algebra of its derived $GL_n$-representation variety of arXiv:1112.1449 from algebras $A$ to perfect stacks $X$ over characteristic 0 fields. In the case of a quasi-projective classical scheme $X$, we show that $\mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$ admits a subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)\subset \mathscr{Rep}_n(X)$, which is in fact represented by a derived scheme almost of finite type. We further construct a Fourier-Mukai integral transform between the derived categories of quasi-coherent sheaves on $X$ and $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ which induces a trace map at the level of Hochschild homology generalizing the trace morphism constructed in arXiv:1112.1449 (for finitely presented commutative algebras). We show that the subfunctor $\operatorname{Quot}^{n,\text{fr}}_{\mathscr{O}_X^n}(X)$ is a derived enhancement of the framed locus of the Quot scheme of points and that this derived scheme is a $GL_n$-torsor over the stack of coherent length $n$ torsion sheaves. Hence, this stack is an analog of the derived character stack for quasi-projective schemes, and we show that for smooth, Calabi-Yau $X$, it inherits a shifted symplectic structure in the sense of arXiv:1111.3209 from the one constructed in arXiv:1812.11913 on the moduli stack of perfect complexes with proper support. This structure is shown to give a generalization of the classical symplectic structure on character varieties of surfaces of genus 1 constructed by Goldman \cite{gold}.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Erlikhman

item.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02043v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
item.dc:creator: Baoyu Zhang, Shengmin Zhang

item.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.05271v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Brou\'{e}--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.
item.dc:creator: Xin Huang, Hanxiao Li
